findings.message: `load_config` directly uses `read_to_string` on a path built from `project_root` without rejecting symlinked ancestors or the config file itself. A symlinked `.harness`, `config`, or TOML file can redirect configuration reads outside the project root.

`configure_sccache` creates `.cache` and writes `sccache.env` without any symlink-boundary checks. A symlinked `.cache` directory or `sccache.env` file can cause the adapter to overwrite data outside `project_root`.

`apply_cleanup` passes each joined cleanup root to `empty_directory` without rejecting symlinked project-root ancestors or the cleanup root itself. `create_dir_all`/`read_dir` can therefore operate through a symlink and remove contents from an external directory.

The configuration loader uses unbounded `std::fs::read_to_string`, so a sufficiently large or continuously supplied configuration file is read without a size limit. The disk-maintenance boundary should use a bounded reader and fail closed when the configured limit is exceeded.

`load_config` reads a path derived from `project_root` without rejecting symlinked ancestors or the config file itself. A symlinked `.harness`, `config`, or TOML file can redirect configuration reads outside the project root.
`configure_sccache` writes `.cache/sccache.env` without symlink-boundary checks. A symlinked `.cache` directory or `sccache.env` file can cause the adapter to overwrite data outside `project_root`.

`apply_cleanup` passes joined cleanup roots to `empty_directory` without rejecting symlinked project-root ancestors or cleanup roots. `create_dir_all`/`read_dir` can operate through a symlink and remove contents from an external directory.

The configuration loader uses unbounded `std::fs::read_to_string`, so arbitrarily large configuration input is read without a size limit. Use a bounded reader and fail closed when the limit is exceeded.

`O_NOFOLLOW` protects only the final path component. After `reject_symlinks_up_to_root` finishes, an already-checked ancestor of `project_root` can be swapped to a symlink before this `open`; resolution then follows that symlink and anchors the descriptor outside the intended tree. Both cleanup and sccache writes consequently retain a TOCTOU escape. Open the path component-by-component from a stable descriptor with no-follow semantics (or an equivalent fail-closed API), and add an ancestor-swap regression test.

The iterative traversal now collects every directory entry into `Vec<CString>` before deleting anything. A sufficiently wide cleanup directory therefore causes unbounded memory growth and can terminate the process through OOM instead of returning a typed adapter error; nested wide directories compound this across active frames. Preserve bounded streaming or process entries in bounded batches.

findings.message: CN-02 は feature 無効 binary の dry 系コマンドについて silent skip または自動 fallback を一律禁止していますが、新設された IN-07/AC-07 は DRY gate 評価点で `enabled: false` の場合に semantic-dup を実行せず通過することを要求しています。gate 評価点も dry 系入口に含まれるため、制約と新しい受入契約が矛盾し、後続フェーズがどちらを実装すべきか決定できません。

`maintenance.rs` imports `CleanupExecutionMode` directly from `usecase` in production code. This violates the CLI dependency boundary: application types must be exposed through `cli_driver` (or the composition root), with the bin limited to parsing, typed driver input construction, and dispatch. Re-export the mode from `cli_driver` or make it part of a CLI-driver-owned input type.

`MaintenanceDriver::handle` dispatches `DryRun` to `query_service` while the other runtime input variants invoke `command_service`. This newly introduced primary adapter therefore selects between separate interactors, violating the cli_driver requirement that a Driver delegate to one use-case service. Move the command/query selection behind a single use-case application service or expose separate one-service Drivers.
findings.category: handle not delegating to single use case

findings.message: `cli_composition::DupIndexBuildInput` is a lightweight DTO containing only two `PathBuf` fields, yet it is the sole input DTO marked `delete`; the sibling semantic-dup input DTOs remain. `IN-01` only grounds gating infrastructure's heavyweight dependencies and does not justify removing this DTO, contradicting the briefing's explicit statement that input DTOs remain outside the catalogue. Remove this tombstone.

`MaintenanceDriver` explicitly owns both `DiskMaintenanceCommandService` and `DiskMaintenanceQueryService` and selects between them in `handle`. This gives one primary adapter responsibility for two independently changing CQRS flows. Split the command and cleanup-plan paths into separate one-service primary adapters and corresponding inputs.

The docs for `cli::commands::semantic_dup_feature_gate::semantic_dup_feature_disabled_exit` reproduce AC-02/CN-02’s behavioral contract—an explicit disabled-feature diagnostic and non-success exit—rather than relying on the existing anchors. Reduce the docs to a local target/operation phrase per `no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`MaintenanceDriver` and `MaintenanceInput` still declare the prohibited combined adapter/input as `action: add` while citing IN-03, AC-03, and AC-04. Those anchors now require one service per driver and separate command/query input families, whereas these entries explicitly retain two services and a combined mode. Transitional intent does not make these references coherent; remove both entries when the source migration lands before approving the catalogue.

The docs for `cli::commands::maintenance::execute` reproduce the amended IN-03/AC-03/AC-04 routing contract by stating that intents are dispatched to distinct command/query drivers. Reduce this to a local identifying phrase and rely on the existing anchors.

`MaintenanceCompositionRoot` restates the upstream command/query separation and single-service-primary-adapter contract in prose. Use a short local noun phrase for the composition root and leave those behavioral requirements to IN-03/AC-03/AC-04.

The docs for `MaintenanceCommandDriver` and `MaintenanceQueryDriver` repeat AC-03's one-service/invoke/render contract, while `MaintenanceCommandInput` and `MaintenanceQueryInput` repeat AC-04's input-family separation. Replace these behavioral sentences with short local type-purpose phrases and rely on the cited anchors.

`cli::commands::dry::execute` is declared as `action: modify`, but the captured rustdoc baseline already has the identical synchronous `fn execute(cmd: DryCommand) -> std::process::ExitCode` signature. T006 changes only its dispatch body, which is not a type-contract mutation; moreover, its `docs` restates the IN-02/IN-07 behavior. Remove this entry (or use `reference` only if edge exposure is genuinely required).
findings.category: action incoherent with the diff / upstream restatement

findings.message: The delete tombstone `cli::commands::dry::execute_dry_check_approved` is grounded only in IN-01, which concerns optional infrastructure dependencies and is unrelated to consolidating check-approved dispatch. The deletion introduced by T006 should cite the gate-evaluation contract in IN-07/AC-07.

`SemanticDupCommandFamily::Dry` still represents the whole dry family while `semantic_dup_feature_disabled_exit` accepts it, so the type permits check-approved to be treated as a direct feature-disabled command and fail before config evaluation. The exclusions at lines 94 and 645 exist only as prose and also restate IN-07 downstream. Encode only direct commands in the selector—for example explicit Write/Results/FixLocal variants—or otherwise narrow the helper so check-approved is unrepresentable.

`FeatureDisabledDryGateDriver`'s `docs` repeats the behavioral boundary that check-approved is exposed while other semantic-dup paths are excluded. Its declared `handle(DryCheckApprovedDriverInput)` shape already identifies that responsibility; replace the behavioral restatement with a short type-purpose phrase and retain the IN-07/AC-07 references.

`FeatureDisabledDryGateInteractor`'s `docs` reproduces IN-07/AC-07's complete algorithm and outcome mapping (`disabled` → Approved, `enabled` → feature-disabled Failure). Per `no-upstream-restatement.md`, keep only a short type-purpose phrase and let `spec_refs` carry this behavioral contract.

`CleanupScope::try_new` accepts `target/.` (and similar `CurDir` aliases) and preserves the uncanonicalized `PathBuf`; `CleanupScopeSet::try_new` therefore treats `target` and `target/.` as distinct even though they address the same cleanup target. This violates the documented duplicate-free invariant and can cause the same directory to be processed twice.

`CleanupScope::try_new("src")` や `CleanupScope::try_new(".git")` が成功します。IN-03/AC-03 は掃除範囲を `target/` と `.cache/` に限定していますが、後続処理は受理されたディレクトリの内容を削除するため、設定ミスでソースや Git メタデータを消失できます。先頭 component を `target` または `.cache` に限定し、その他は fail-closed で拒否してください。

`trimmed.len()` はバイト長なので、末尾が複数バイト文字の入力（例: `"10Ｇ"`）では `len - 1` が UTF-8 境界にならず `split_at` が panic します。任意の不正設定値は `InvalidCacheSize` に変換すべきであり、これは `coding-principles.md` §No Panics in Library Code に違反します。`split_at_checked` または安全な ASCII suffix 解析を使用してください。

`prepare-local-cache-dirs` invokes `cargo run` without clearing `RUSTC_WRAPPER`; this bootstrap command can itself run through sccache before `configure-sccache` has established the current configuration, leaving the first cache-generating workload outside the intended initialization/propagation path. Run it with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` as required by the briefing’s bootstrap wiring.

The maintenance task cleans the default `target/` and then immediately invokes `cargo run` again. Because the first cleanup removes the CLI binary and Cargo fingerprints, the configure step recompiles the CLI and repopulates `target/`, so the task finishes with build artifacts it promised to remove. Run configuration without rebuilding inside a cleanup scope, for example via a preserved/prebuilt executable.

Replacing `--all-features` with only `--features semantic-dup` drops existing CI coverage for independent features such as `cli_composition/test-support` and `infrastructure/test-helpers`; tests guarded by `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]` are now skipped. Preserve `--all-features`—which already enables semantic-dup—or explicitly include every previously covered feature.

`mktemp` creates the destination file without execute permission, and plain `cp` overwrites its contents while retaining that existing mode. Consequently the first `"$CLI_BIN"` invocation fails with `Permission denied`, so `cargo make maintenance` never performs cleanup. Copy into a previously nonexistent path or install the binary with an explicit executable mode.

The temporary executable is placed under `${TMPDIR}` without ensuring that location is outside the configured cleanup roots. With a repository-local `TMPDIR` such as `.cache/tmp` or `target/tmp`, the cleanup invocation deletes its own copied executable, and the subsequent configure invocation fails because the path no longer exists. Place the survivor binary in a validated location excluded from cleanup.
ADR に `## Reassess When` セクションがなく、決定を見直す具体的なトリガーが記録されていません。

This generated env file becomes a second source of truth for the cache limit. Compose and CI read this hard-coded value directly, while the supported user override lives in `.harness/config/disk-maintenance.toml`; nothing in this scope verifies they remain synchronized, and CI starts Compose without regenerating the file. A later config-only override can therefore pass CI while CI still uses the stale committed limit, and normal preparation can stage generated cache state via `git add-all`. Keep the limit single-sourced: generate and ignore this file in every execution path (including CI), or add a fail-closed synchronization gate.

This step invokes `cargo make` on the bare `ubuntu-latest` host before the tools image is built, but the workflow never installs `cargo-make` or the repository's pinned Rust toolchain; `cargo-make` is installed only inside the Docker image. A clean GitHub runner will therefore fail here (or use an incompatible ambient Rust installation) before reaching Buildx. Keep the directory-only host preparation here and generate the env file after loading the tools image, or explicitly install/pin the required host tooling first.
